newsitem.title: UK: BP, Greenpeace meet to discuss Atlantic oil projects.
newsitem.headline: BP, Greenpeace meet to discuss Atlantic oil projects.

text.p: Oil major British Petroleum has met with Greenpeace to discuss the environmental group's concerns over oil developments on Britain's Atlantic margin, representatives of both sides said on Tuesday.
"We did have a briefing on our operations West of Shetland with Greenpeace, and we have written to them," said a spokesman for BP.
Sarah Burton, campaigns director for Greenpeace, said that a meeting had taken place on February 21.
But she said rumours that Greenpeace was to take direct action to sabotage BP's operations in the Atlantic area west of the Shetland Islands were started by the oil company.
"It's clear that some of the rumours were started by BP. But we haven't made any threats of direct action," Burton said.
She added that the organisation could not rule out future action as it does not discuss future plans.
"We are opposed to (BP's) development and exploration in the Atlantic frontier," she said.
BP is operator of the Foinaven field which is due on stream in a matter of weeks and expected to reach peak production of 120,000 barrels per day.
A second field, Schiehallion, is due onstream in mid-1998, while earlier this month BP announced the discovery of a third field, Suilven.
